method: Twenty-five isolated same-image service-account suites sent valid fixture requests through the Keycloak client. This historical action-route set contains 184 state-changing mutations and one read-only POST client-description converter; it also includes the side-effecting GET reload-keys route. Many stateful fixtures had related readbacks; some action/export routes had only response-status checks. The earlier bodyless route matrix remains separate. HTTP success does not imply every possible payload or rollback behavior. The public workflow API was tested separately. The latest suites used local SMTP and HTTP sinks to check email delivery, organization invitations, revocation callbacks, identity-provider metadata fetch and key reload; they also verified session deletion and certificate upload readbacks. Both bundled OpenAPI versions omit the multipart certificate upload body, so the client adds an exact-route correction.
